lines.text: The first Spanish city of the Americas, a hard-won independence, a harsh dictator, and a passion for baseball and music. This is the Dominican Republic.
Long before Europeans came, the Taino lived on the island of Hispaniola, farming, fishing and trading by canoe.
Columbus arrived, and in 1496 the Spanish founded Santo Domingo, the oldest European city in the Americas.
There, in 1511, the explorer's son Diego Columbus began his palace, the Alcazar de Colon.
A few years later work began on the first cathedral of the Americas, in the heart of the city.
Centuries passed under Spain and France. In 1813 Juan Pablo Duarte was born, the man who would dream of a free republic.
In 1822 neighbouring Haiti took control of the whole island, and ruled it for twenty-two years.
In 1844 the east of the island broke away, and the Dominican Republic was born.
Freedom had to be defended. War with Haiti went on for years before independence was secure.
Around then a fast, joyful dance music took shape. Merengue would become the sound of the nation.
In 1891 Rafael Trujillo was born. He would seize control in 1930 and rule the country with an iron hand for three decades.
Joaquin Balaguer would serve Trujillo, and later be president himself for twenty-two years.
In 1916 United States marines landed, and ran the country for eight years.
In 1937, on Trujillo's orders, thousands of Haitians living near the border were killed.
In 1957 Juan Luis Guerra was born. His merengue and bachata would win Grammys and fans across the world.
Around 1960, bachata grew in the countryside, guitar songs of love and heartbreak, now danced everywhere.
That same year, three Mirabal sisters who opposed Trujillo were murdered. Their memory lives on in a world day against violence toward women.
Trujillo was killed in 1961. Four years later civil war broke out, and the United States sent in troops.
Luis Abinader, born in 1967, would be elected president in 2020.
Baseball became a national passion. Pedro Martinez grew up to be one of the greatest pitchers the game has seen.
Vladimir Guerrero would hit his way into the Hall of Fame, one of many Dominican stars.
And David Ortiz, Big Papi, would become a hero to the fans of the Boston Red Sox.
From Taino villages to baseball diamonds, the Dominican Republic's story is one of survival and rhythm.
